subject: Post-demo costing follow-up — feature-slice unit econ & CAC payback
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: demo & quick sizing for feature slices (token bands / $/1M targets)

Hi Alex & Priya — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a pilot pricing worksheet: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: embed guided check-in and automated appointment reminders in pilot region (~US west).
- Target feature set (MVP slice): 1) appointment rename/confirmation chat flow, 2) automated pre-visit follow-ups, 3) post-visit NPS micro-survey.
- Expected traffic: you estimated 50–150k end-users in pilot cohort; we need concrete monthly token estimate per feature.

Primary asks & next steps (what we need from LumaHealth to size $/feature and CAC payback):
1) Token/session estimate per feature (average tokens in/out; typical session windows). If you have sample transcripts, paste one.
2) Target $/1M tokens band (budget range) — you mentioned a $/month budget but not the $/1M token anchoring.
3) CAC / conversion assumptions for the pilot (how you think value will translate to customer revenue or retention — we’ll map to payback).

What Redwood will deliver after we get the items above:
- A per-feature unit economic model: $/feature (inference cost), contribution margin at a couple of pricing scenarios, and CAC payback curves.
- Recommended token banding and suggested model variant (latency vs cost tradeoffs) for each feature.

I’ve attached an empty costing workbook (LumaHealth_MVP_feature_slice_cost_model.xlsx) with tabs for tokens, model choices, and payback. Can you and Priya fill the token estimates by EOD Tuesday PT? We’ll turn that into a $/feature and a 90-day payback plan.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo & quick sizing for feature slices (token bands / $/1M targets)

Thanks Neha — good meeting. Quick answers inline and a few clarifications: 

Tokens/session (ballpark, avg across our current flows):
- Appointment confirmation chat (2–3 user turns + system prompts): ~220 tokens/session out, ~180 tokens/session in => ~400 tokens total
- Pre-visit follow-ups (single outbound reminder + 1 user reply option): ~100 tokens/session
- Post-visit NPS micro-survey (3 questions + short comment): ~140 tokens/session

Monthly usage expectation for pilot (we’ll run in two clinics):
- Active users/month: ~120k combined clinics
- Adoption target for messaging flows: 12% initial (we know adoption will ramp) => ~14.4k engaged users/month

So estimated monthly tokens by feature (rough):
- Confirmations: 14.4k * 400 = 5.76M tokens
- Pre-visit reminders: 14.4k * 100 = 1.44M tokens
- NPS micro-survey: 14.4k * 140 = 2.016M tokens
- Total ~9.216M tokens/month

Budget: We have an initial pilot budget scoped at $6k–$12k / month for inference and integration costs (not including your platform fee). If you can show a unit $/feature scenario that lands < $0.50 contribution cost per engaged user for the most common flows, that’d be reasonable.

Happy to fill the attached sheet with these estimates — forwarding to Priya to confirm exact session lengths and to drop one sample transcript.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Product Manager | LumaHealth
alex.turner@lumahealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: demo & quick sizing for feature slices (token bands / $/1M targets)

Great numbers Alex — thanks for the quick lift. I sketched a lightweight unit-econ model below to map your ranges into $/feature and CAC payback (assumptions noted). Use this as a sanity check; we’ll formalize in the workbook once Priya shares the transcript.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model inference cost baseline: $12 / 1M tokens (optimized quantized variant, mixed-precision)
- Redwood platform fee (hosted) & overhead: $1,500 / month (pilot minimum)
- Customer monetization lift from flows: incremental LTV per engaged user = $4 (mix of retention + fewer no-shows)
- CAC allocated to this pilot: $36,000 (customer acquisition program for pilot cohort) => monthly amortized CAC over 12 months = $3,000 / month (for payback curve)

Using Alex’s token projections (~9.216M tokens/month):
- Monthly inference cost = 9.216 * $12 / 1M = $110.59 (wait calculation: 9.216 * 12 = 110.592 -> actually $110.59)
- Add platform fee = $1,500 => total monthly run cost = $1,610.59
- Cost per engaged user (14.4k engaged users): $1,610.59 / 14,400 ≈ $0.112 / engaged user
- If we apportion cost per feature (weighted by tokens):
  - Confirmations (5.76M tokens; 62.5% of tokens) => $0.07 / engaged user equivalent
  - Pre-visit reminders (1.44M; 15.6%) => $0.018
  - NPS (2.016M; 21.9%) => $0.025

Contribution margin (per engaged user) at two price points:
- If Luma charges $1.00 value-based fee (or attributes $1.00 of LTV) => contribution = $1.00 - $0.112 = $0.888 => ~89% contribution margin vs inference+platform cost.
- If Luma attributes $0.25 value => contribution = $0.25 - $0.112 = $0.138 => ~55% margin.

CAC payback (simple):
- Monthly incremental gross contribution = engaged users * contribution per user. At conservative $0.25 value: 14,400 * $0.138 ≈ $1,987 / month.
- With monthly amortized CAC $3,000, payback time ~1.5 months. If we include full CAC bucket (not amortized) payback = 15 months; so allocation matters.

Notes & questions:
- The $12 / 1M tokens assumption is model-dependent — if you need a lower-cost model we can propose a quantized variant that could push to $6–8 / 1M tokens with slightly higher latency.
- The platform fee dominates the per-user cost at low volumes. For pilots, we can discuss a reduced pilot fee or credits to reach a target $/feature goal.

I can drop these values into the workbook and model a breakpoint table showing target unit price vs payback months. Ben

--
Ben Carter
Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0142

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: demo & quick sizing for feature slices (token bands / $/1M targets)

Alex — quick internal note and potential concession for pilot economics.

We reviewed Ben’s sketch and Neha’s ask. For a two-clinic pilot we’re prepared to offer either: 
A) Pilot discount model: 50% off platform fee for first 3 months (reduces platform fee to $750/mo) + standard $12 / 1M tokens rate.
B) Lower token rate: $8 / 1M tokens, platform fee unchanged, for pilots that agree to a 6-month committed usage band.

Both options aim to get your $/engaged-user under $0.20 in month 1, then show payback <3 months under conservative LTV assumptions.

If either is attractive, we’ll prepare a short amendment (term sheet) and loop in procurement. Otherwise we’ll model a custom hybrid.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
